mainTopic: Chopping wood on יום טוב, making a hole to reach stored produce, and untying rope seals on שבת and יום טוב
overview: The גמרא asks how the משנה can say 'one may not chop at all' and then describe how one may chop. שמואל answers that the משנה is missing a line. מוקצה wood may not be chopped at all, while a beam that broke before יום טוב may be chopped, but only with a קופיץ, and a ברייתא supports this. רב adds that the narrow side of a קרדום is allowed and its broad side is forbidden. Each side of a two-sided tool is judged by itself. A new משנה teaches that produce may be taken through a hole in a storage house, and רבי מאיר allows making the hole on purpose. The גמרא explains that the wall is loose bricks, and that רבי מאיר's leniency applies only on יום טוב, not שבת. שמואל then rules that rope seals attached to the ground may only be untied, on both שבת and יום טוב. A ברייתא that allows cutting them on יום טוב is assigned to רבי מאיר. But another ברייתא says the חכמים agree with רבי מאיר here, and the answer to that challenge comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה can forbid chopping entirely and then go on to describe permitted ways of chopping.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: But didn't you say in the first part of the משנה that one may not chop at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the משנה's opening line seems to forbid all chopping. Yet the משנה later talks about chopping with a קופיץ, which sounds like chopping is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא states 'אין מבקעין' with no conditions. The סיפא lists forbidden tools and ends with 'only with a קופיץ,' which implies some chopping is permitted. Both cannot be true unless the משנה is talking about different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion on the משנה
But didn't you say? (introduces a contradiction)
The first clause of a משנה
Chopping or splitting wood
At all

phrases.english: GEMARA:
But didn't you say in the first clause
one may not chop at all?
phrases.notes: The משנה's opening line seems to be an absolute ban.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the משנה's wording
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רישא forbids all chopping, while the סיפא assumes chopping with a קופיץ is allowed, so the two clauses contradict.

steps.title: The משנה is missing a line: some wood may be chopped, with a cleaver
steps.stepSummary: שמואל fills in the missing case. מוקצה beams may never be chopped. A beam broken before יום טוב may be chopped, but only with a קופיץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it teaches. One may not chop from a pile of beams, nor from a beam that broke on יום טוב. But one may chop from a beam that broke before יום טוב. And when one does chop, it may not be with an ax, a sickle, or a saw, but only with a cleaver.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל resolves the contradiction by saying the משנה is talking about two different kinds of wood. One kind may never be chopped; the other may be chopped, but only in a changed way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'not at all' applies to wood that is מוקצה: construction beams, or a beam that only became firewood on יום טוב itself. A beam that broke on ערב יום טוב was already ready for burning, so chopping it is allowed. Even then one must use a קופיץ rather than normal weekday tools.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing something, and this is what it teaches
A pile of beams set aside for building
A beam that broke
The day before the festival
Ax, sickle, saw (regular weekday chopping tools)
A cleaver (a butcher's chopping knife)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate rules here. WHICH wood may be chopped is a question of מוקצה. HOW it may be chopped (only with a קופיץ) is about avoiding the usual weekday manner. Do not mix the two reasons.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading turns one seemingly contradictory משנה into two clear layers: what may be chopped, and how.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The mishna is incomplete
and this is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְבַקְּעִין מִן הַסְּוָאר שֶׁל קוֹרוֹת,
phrases.english: One may not chop from the pile of beams,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מִן הַקּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: nor from a beam that broke on the Festival.
But one may chop from a beam
that broke on the eve of the Festival.
phrases.notes: This is the line the משנה was 'missing.'

phrases.english: And when they do chop —
one may not chop with an ax,
nor with a sickle, nor with a saw,
but only with a cleaver.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation (חסורי מחסרא) that splits the משנה into two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbids all chopping, yet also permits chopping, which is self-contradictory.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban on chopping applies to מוקצה wood. Wood broken before יום טוב may be chopped, but only with a קופיץ.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל's reading
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also forbids chopping beams from the pile or beams broken on יום טוב, and gives the reason: they are not prepared (מוכן).
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: One may not chop wood, neither from the pile of beams nor from a beam that broke on יום טוב, because it is not prepared.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches שמואל's explanation, including the reason behind the ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spells out that the reason is 'שאינו מן המוכן': the wood was not ready for use before יום טוב. This confirms that the 'no chopping at all' is about מוקצה, which is exactly how שמואל split the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way (in a ברייתא)
Wood
Prepared or designated before יום טוב (the opposite of מוקצה)

steps.whatToRemember: Chopping is banned for wood that was not 'מוכן' before יום טוב. Wood that was prepared may be chopped, but only with a קופיץ.

phrases.english: This is also taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְבַקְּעִין עֵצִים לֹא מִן הַסְּוָאר שֶׁל קוֹרוֹת
phrases.english: One may not chop wood, neither from the pile of beams

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מִן הַקּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: nor from the beam that broke on the Festival,
because it is not from what is prepared.

steps.raayaObject: שמואל's reading that the ban applies to מוקצה wood
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that gives the reason 'שאינו מן המוכן'

steps.title: The ax ban applies only to its broad side
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that the ban on chopping with a קרדום applies only to its broad (female) side. Its narrow (male) side is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'not with an ax.' רב חיננא בר שלמיא said in the name of רב: They taught this only about its female (broad) side, but with its male (narrow) side it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'not with an ax,' and רב narrows that rule. Only the ax's usual chopping side is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Chopping with the broad side is the normal weekday way, so it is forbidden. The narrow side is an unusual way to chop, much like a קופיץ, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this (rule) about...
The 'female' side: the broad blade of the ax
The 'male' side: the narrow, pointed side of the ax
Permitted

phrases.english: 'Nor with an ax.'
phrases.notes: Quoting the words of the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥinnana bar Shelemya said in the name of Rav:
They taught this only regarding its female (broad) side,
but with its male (narrow) side, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which wood may be chopped to a detail about the forbidden tools
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on the קרדום applies only to its broad side. The narrow side is permitted.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious from the cleaver rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב needed to teach this, since the משנה already permits a קופיץ, and the ax's narrow side works like one.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! We already learned in the משנה that a cleaver is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's statement as unnecessary, since it seems to add nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a narrow-edged קופיץ is permitted, then the narrow side of an ax should obviously be permitted too. So רב's statement looks redundant.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (challenges a statement as unnecessary)
We learned (in a משנה)

phrases.english: It is obvious,
we learned 'with a cleaver'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רב's statement in step 4 was needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already permits a קופיץ, and the ax's narrow side is the same kind of edge, so רב's ruling adds nothing.

steps.title: A two-sided tool might have seemed fully forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the new point. One might have thought that because one side of the ax is forbidden, the whole tool is forbidden. רב teaches that the narrow side is still allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: This applies only to a cleaver by itself. But a tool that is an ax on one side and a cleaver on the other, I might say: since this side is forbidden, that side is forbidden too. So רב teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' challenge by showing what mistake רב's statement prevents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain קופיץ is clearly fine. But an ax has a forbidden side attached to it, so one might reason (מגו) that the whole tool is forbidden. רב teaches that each side is judged by how it is used, so the narrow side is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (introduces the mistaken assumption)
These words apply only to...
By itself
Since (linking reasoning: because X, therefore also Y)
Side
He teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: Chopping on יום טוב: מוקצה wood may never be chopped. Prepared wood may be chopped only in an unusual way, with a קופיץ or even the narrow side of an ax, but not with the ax's broad side, a saw, or a sickle.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
This applies only to a cleaver by itself,
but a tool that is an ax and a cleaver, I would say:
since this side is forbidden —
that side is also forbidden,
he therefore teaches us otherwise.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the necessity of the statement by identifying a plausible mistaken assumption (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the ax's broad side is forbidden, the whole two-sided tool, including its narrow side, would be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each side is judged on its own. The narrow side, used like a קופיץ, is permitted even though it is attached to a forbidden side.

steps.title: A second version: רב's teaching attached to the cleaver clause
steps.stepSummary: Some place רב's teaching on the משנה's words 'but with a קופיץ.' In this version רב says the permission covers only the narrow side, and the broad side is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this on the end of the משנה, 'but rather with a cleaver.' רב חיננא בר שלמיא said in the name of רב: they taught this only for its narrow (male) side. With its broad (female) side, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of רב's teaching from step 4. This time it is attached to the permission clause, and it stresses what stays forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רב read the ban on the קרדום and said the narrow side is allowed. In this version, רב reads the permission for a קופיץ and says that on a two-sided tool, only the narrow side is allowed. The practical rule is the same. Only the emphasis changes, from 'the narrow side is allowed' to 'the broad side is still forbidden.'

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it (an alternate version)
On the latter clause (the end part of the משנה)
The 'male' side, meaning the narrow edge of the tool
The 'female' side, meaning the broad edge of the tool

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions lead to the same practical rule: the narrow side is allowed and the broad side is forbidden. The two versions differ only in which line of the משנה רב is commenting on.

phrases.english: And some teach it on the latter clause:
"but rather with a cleaver."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chinnana bar Shelemya said in the name of Rav:
They taught this only with its male (narrow) side,
but with its female (broad) side, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts רב's teaching from step 4 as a second version attached to a different clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a two-sided tool, the permission to chop applies only to the narrow side. The broad side is forbidden.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious from the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this second version is obvious, because the משנה already forbids a קרדום.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious! Didn't we learn in the משנה, 'not with an ax'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges this version of רב. It asks why we need him to tell us the broad side is forbidden, when the משנה already says so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, the question was why רב needed to teach that the narrow side is allowed. Here the question flips: why teach that the broad side is forbidden? The broad side is exactly a קרדום, which the משנה already bans.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious (an objection that a teaching adds nothing)
An ax, which has a broad blade

phrases.english: It is obvious! Didn't we learn "not with an ax"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the second version of רב adds anything
steps.kashyaTarget: The second version of רב's teaching
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The broad side is a קרדום, and the משנה already forbids a קרדום, so רב's teaching seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The new point: one allowed side does not permit the whole tool
steps.stepSummary: One might have thought that on a tool that is both cleaver and ax, the allowed narrow side makes the broad side allowed too. רב teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: that ban applies to a plain ax. But a tool that is both a cleaver and an ax, you might say, since this side is permitted, the other side is permitted too. So רב teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection by naming the mistake רב is preventing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's ban could be read as covering only a plain ax. For a combined tool, one might reason that the allowed side 'pulls along' the other side (מגו). רב teaches that this is wrong: the broad side stays forbidden even on a combined tool. This mirrors step 6 in reverse. There, the fear was that the forbidden side would make the whole tool forbidden. Here, the fear is that the allowed side would make the whole tool allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces the mistaken assumption)
Since; because of (one part affects the other)
Side
It teaches us (the new point)

steps.whatToRemember: On a two-sided tool, each side is judged by itself on יום טוב. The narrow side is allowed and the broad side is forbidden. Neither side changes the status of the other.

phrases.english: Lest you say: these words apply to a plain ax,
but a tool that is both a cleaver and an ax,
I would say: since this side is permitted,
this other side is also permitted,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a mistaken assumption (הוה אמינא) that the teaching prevents
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the narrow side of a combined tool is allowed, the broad side would be allowed too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The broad side stays forbidden even on a combined tool.

steps.title: New משנה: taking produce through a hole in a storage house
steps.stepSummary: If a sealed house full of produce gets a hole, one may take produce through the hole on יום טוב. רבי מאיר says one may even make a hole on purpose to take it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A house that is full of produce, and a hole formed in it. One may take produce from the place of the hole. רבי מאיר says: one may even make a hole from the start and take.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic: getting food out of a sealed storage house on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allows using a hole that formed by itself. The produce does not count as מוקצה just because it was locked away. רבי מאיר goes further and allows making the hole on purpose (לכתחילה).

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A hole formed (by itself)
Makes a hole (on purpose)
From the start; on purpose, as a first step

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
A house that is full of produce, and a hole formed in it,
one may take produce through the place of the hole.
Rabbi Meir says:
One may even make a hole from the start and take produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce may be taken through a hole that formed in the house. רבי מאיר allows making the hole on purpose.

steps.title: Isn't making a hole taking down a structure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי מאיר can allow making a hole, since that seems to be taking apart a building.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why is this allowed? He is taking apart a tent (a structure)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a hole in a wall or roof looks like סתירה, taking down a structure, which is a forbidden מלאכה. So how can רבי מאיר allow it even on יום טוב?

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
Why?
Taking apart a tent or structure (forbidden סתירה)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Why is this allowed?
But he is taking apart a tent!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי מאיר's ruling in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's permission to make a hole on purpose
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Making a hole is סתירה, taking down a structure, which is forbidden.

steps.title: שמואל: the wall is just loosely stacked bricks
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the case is a wall of loose bricks with no mortar, which does not count as a building.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחומי בר אדא said in the name of שמואל: the case is bricks just stacked on each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bricks stacked without mortar are not a real structure. So removing them is not סתירה. רבי מאיר's ruling is limited to this kind of wall.

keyTerms.meaning: Bricks placed loosely on top of each other, with no mortar
Bricks

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נְחוּמִי בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Nechumi bar Adda said that Shmuel said:
The case is bricks loosely stacked on each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נְחוּמִי בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hole is made in a real built wall, which would be סתירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wall is loose bricks, which is not a building.

steps.title: רב נחמן: stacked bricks are מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל from רב נחמן, who rules that once bricks are arranged in a stack, they are מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב נחמן said: bricks left over from a building may be moved on שבת, since they are fit to sit on. Once he stacked them in rows, he has certainly set them aside (made them מוקצה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's answer using a ruling of רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Loose leftover bricks are useful as seats, so they may be moved. Once someone stacks them, he shows he has set them aside for building, so they become מוקצה. If so, how can one move the stacked bricks to make a hole?

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (introduces a challenge)
To move them
He arranged them in rows or stacks
He set them aside (made them מוקצה)

phrases.english: Is that so? But didn't Rav Nachman say:
These bricks that were left over from a building,
it is permitted to move them on Shabbat,
since they are fit to sit on.
If he stacked them, he has certainly set them aside!

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's explanation that the wall is loose bricks
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Stacked bricks are מוקצה according to רב נחמן, so removing them should still be forbidden.

steps.title: רבי זירא: יום טוב is different from שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that רבי מאיר's permission is for יום טוב only. רב נחמן's ruling is about שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: they said this about יום טוב, but not about שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the conflict by splitting the two rulings between יום טוב and שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן spoke about שבת, when stacked bricks stay מוקצה. רבי מאיר spoke about יום טוב, where the rules are more lenient in order to get food. So making the hole is allowed only on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Festival day, when preparing food is allowed
Shabbat, which has stricter rules

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב אָמְרוּ, אֲבָל לֹא בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: They said it about a Festival, but not about Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: בְּיוֹם טוֹב אָמְרוּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (יום טוב versus שבת)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר's permission would clash with רב נחמן's rule about stacked bricks.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר permits only on יום טוב. רב נחמן's rule applies to שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms: יום טוב only
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי מאיר's ruling and adds that it applies on יום טוב and not on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא. רבי מאיר says: one may even make a hole from the start and take. They said this about יום טוב, but not about שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבי זירא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states רבי מאיר's ruling and openly limits it to יום טוב. This confirms that רבי זירא's distinction is not just a guess.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a supporting source)
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר allows making a hole in a wall of loose bricks to take out produce, but only on יום טוב. On שבת, stacked bricks are מוקצה and may not be moved.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Rabbi Meir says:
One may even make a hole from the start and take produce.

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב אָמְרוּ, אֲבָל לֹא בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: They said it about a Festival, but not about Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי זירא's answer in step 14
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's distinction between יום טוב and שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי מאיר with the limit to יום טוב

steps.title: שמואל's rule for rope seals on the ground and on vessels
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that ground seals may only be untied. Vessel seals may be untied, unraveled, or cut. This applies equally on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: if rope seals are attached to the ground, you may untie them, but you may not unravel or cut them. If they are on vessels, you may untie, unravel, or cut them. This is the same on שבת and on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a new rule about rope ties that close doors. His rule depends on whether the door is attached to the ground or is part of a vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A door attached to the ground counts like part of a building. Cutting or unraveling its rope would be like taking the building apart (סותר), so only untying is allowed. Vessels have no building prohibition, so anything is allowed, and שמואל says this holds on both שבת and יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Seals: knotted ropes that tie a door closed
Ground: something attached to the ground
Unties the knot
Unravels the rope into its strands
Cuts the rope
Vessels, such as a cupboard or chest

steps.confusionAlert: The key point is that שמואל treats שבת and יום טוב exactly the same. That is what the next step attacks.

phrases.english: Shmuel said: seals that are attached to the ground —

phrases.aramaic: מַתִּיר, אֲבָל לֹא מַפְקִיעַ וְלֹא חוֹתֵךְ.
phrases.english: one may untie, but not unravel and not cut.
Those on vessels — one may untie, unravel, and cut,
the same on Shabbat and on Yom Tov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from bricks and making a hole to a related topic: rope seals and taking apart something attached to the ground.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ground seals: untie only. Vessel seals: untie, unravel, or cut. No difference between שבת and יום טוב.

steps.title: A ברייתא allows cutting ground seals on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows only untying ground seals on שבת, but allows unraveling and cutting them on יום טוב. This contradicts שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא objects from a ברייתא: for seals attached to the ground, on שבת you may untie but not unravel or cut. On יום טוב you may untie, unravel, and cut!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that splits the law between שבת and יום טוב. That goes against שמואל, who said they are the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said ground seals may never be cut, on either day. The ברייתא says that on יום טוב cutting is allowed. So the ברייתא directly contradicts the "same on שבת and יום טוב" part of שמואל's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: They objected: a challenge brought from a תנאי source

phrases.english: They objected: seals attached to the ground, on Shabbat —

phrases.aramaic: מַתִּיר אֲבָל לֹא מַפְקִיעַ וְלֹא חוֹתֵךְ.
phrases.english: one may untie, but not unravel and not cut.
On Yom Tov — one may untie, unravel, and cut!

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that ground seals may not be cut even on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly allows unraveling and cutting ground seals on יום טוב, so שבת and יום טוב are not the same.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, but שמואל follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: שמואל can answer that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who is lenient on יום טוב. The רבנן disagree with רבי מאיר, and שמואל rules like the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this ברייתא? It is רבי מאיר, who said one may even make a hole from the start and take out food. The רבנן disagree with him, and I (שמואל) ruled like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for שמואל. The ברייתא is the opinion of רבי מאיר, and שמואל simply follows the other side, the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (steps 14-15) we learned that רבי מאיר allows making a hole on יום טוב. So it fits that he would also allow cutting ground seals on יום טוב. The רבנן are stricter, and שמואל's rule matches them, so the ברייתא does not disprove him.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this?
Makes a hole (breaks an opening)
From the start: allowed in the first place, not only after the fact
I, who said: the speaker identifies which view he follows

phrases.english: Whose is this? It is Rabbi Meir,
who said: one may even make a hole from the start and take,
and the Rabbis disagree with him,
and I spoke in accordance with the Rabbis.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the source to a specific תנא (רבי מאיר) whose view is disputed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא states the accepted law, which would refute שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is רבי מאיר's view only. שמואל follows the רבנן, who disagree.

steps.title: The Sages agree with רבי מאיר about ground seals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. A ברייתא says the חכמים agree with רבי מאיר on ground seals, so שמואל cannot claim the רבנן disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do the רבנן really disagree with him about seals attached to the ground? But a ברייתא teaches: the חכמים agree with רבי מאיר about ground seals. On שבת one may untie but not unravel or cut, and on יום טוב one may untie, unravel, and cut!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 18. It brings a ברייתא showing that on this topic the רבנן actually agree with רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 depended on the רבנן disagreeing with רבי מאיר. This ברייתא says that about ground seals in particular, the חכמים admit he is right and allow cutting on יום טוב. That leaves שמואל with no תנא who supports him, and this passage ends with this challenge still open.

keyTerms.meaning: But do they really disagree? (a challenging question)
But it was taught in a ברייתא
The Sages agree (concede)

steps.confusionAlert: Even though the רבנן disagree with רבי מאיר about making a hole, this ברייתא says they agree with him about rope seals. One dispute does not mean they disagree on every case.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ בְּחוֹתָמוֹת שֶׁבַּקַּרְקַע?
phrases.english: And do the Rabbis disagree with him regarding seals attached to the ground?
But it was taught: the Sages concede to Rabbi Meir
regarding seals attached to the ground,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת מַתִּיר — אֲבָל לֹא מַפְקִיעַ וְלֹא חוֹתֵךְ,
phrases.english: that on Shabbat one may untie, but not unravel and not cut,
on Yom Tov one may untie, unravel, and cut!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ בְּחוֹתָמוֹת שֶׁבַּקַּרְקַע וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 18 that the רבנן disagree with רבי מאיר about ground seals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly states that the חכמים concede to רבי מאיר about ground seals, so שמואל has no תנא who supports forbidding cutting on יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a fresh defense of שמואל, which must come in the next part of the sugya.
